newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound strengthens further during week.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound strengthens further during week.

text.p: The Lebanese pound continued its steady appreciation against the U.S. dollar in the week ended Friday on a quiet market with a continued oversupply of dollars, dealers said.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,546-1,555.50 pounds per dollar from 1,546.5-1,556 and the dollar again traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.
The central bank bought most of the dollars on offer and commercial banks absorbed only 15-20 percent, dealers said.
"People are not buying dollars and the amounts offered are above the banks' commercial requirements," Talal Abou Zaki, forex manager for Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, told Reuters.
Trade was limited to a very tight band of 10-25 piastres at the bid end of the central bank's intervention band, Abou Zaki said.
After the Bank lowered its bid rate to 1,546 pounds on Tuesday, the dollar traded at 1,546-1,546.25 or 1,546.05-1,546.15, he added.
"The mood is still in favour of the Lebanese pound because people are convinced by the high interest rates on the pound and have no fears about the political or security situation," Abou Zaki said.
